## Highlights since 0.16.13

- **Visual mode for .tex files.** A Source/Visual switch in the .tex tab renders headings, emphasis, math (with your project's macros), lists, figures and captions, \ref and \eqref numbers from the last build, \cite chips and \input links in place, and everything stays editable. Moving the caret into an element shows its source, a single keystroke never leaves an unbalanced brace, and Overleaf sync sees no edits from switching modes. Thanks to @surajinacademia and @Paivel for asking for it.
- **Several projects in one window.** Project tabs sit at the left of the title bar; use "Open in this window" to add one and Ctrl+Tab to move between them. Each project keeps its editor state, and Lattice asks before switching away from a running build, shell or agent turn. Thanks to @surajinacademia for asking for it.
- **Connect your own model endpoint.** In Settings → Agent → Model endpoint, enter an OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible base URL, a key (kept in the macOS Keychain) and model ids, then Test connection. The integrated agent then runs through Pi without installing a CLI, Proofread, Polish and revisions can use the same endpoint, and Pi asks before editing in approval mode. Thanks to @hyzhou-nv for asking for it.

## Notable fixes

- Windows: install TeX Live from the setup dialog. Thanks to @ivanvykopal.
- Windows: Zotero import finds Windows profiles and linked PDFs on drive letters and network (UNC) paths. Thanks to @LucasDavidTPE.
- Editable figures: export each figure for a journal, and the preamble is completed when a drawing changes. Thanks to @Paivel.
- The updater installs the newest release instead of an older offer, so you are not prompted a second time.
- Math preview reads macros with nested braces, \def and \DeclareMathOperator.
- A co-author's file rename on Overleaf is carried over to your local edits.
- Overleaf project downloads show a real progress bar.
- A failing paper no longer rebuilds endlessly when Google Drive, Dropbox or iCloud touch the folder, and the arydshln-after-colortbl error in TeX Live 2026 now comes with a hint.
- PDF text stays smooth when zoomed out on 1x displays. Thanks to @Paivel for the report.
